stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its application in large language model tasks.
The model is associated with key technologies like transformers and safetensors, central to modern NLP.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags such as 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates active community interest and benchmarking activity around a major LLM model.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is optimized for local coding agents and features native support for DFlash and image input via Ollama's MLX engine.

stories.title: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launches to study dark matter and dark energy
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has successfully launched after facing funding and naming changes.
It will travel to the L2 Lagrange point beyond the Moon for its mission.
The telescope is designed to conduct an unprecedented survey of the universe to study dark matter and dark energy.

stories.title: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell are suing Anthropic
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Major music publishers (Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell) are suing Anthropic.
The lawsuit alleges unauthorized use of tens of thousands of copyrighted musical works by Anthropic.
The plaintiffs are seeking substantial damages, potentially up to $150,000 per work.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, indicating a focus on practical LLM deployment.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for persistent AI agents.
The model is designed for complex, multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance using Gemma 4 saw up to 90% speed increase on the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and reduced memory usage for models.
The updated engine also contributes to higher quality outputs from the language models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, offering a faster local AI experience for Mac users.
The feature is currently available in preview, indicating ongoing development and optimization.

stories.title: Trump blacklisting of "woke" Anthropic deemed illegal by federal judge
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A federal judge ruled that a blacklisting action by Trump against Anthropic was illegal.
Anthropic has publicly opposed the development of lethal autonomous warfare and mass surveillance technologies.
The ruling highlights legal challenges surrounding government attempts to restrict AI development based on ideological stances.

stories.title: InstructMesh: Selective Refinement of Generative 3D Models for Fabrication
stories.author: Stefanie Mueller
bullet_points: InstructMesh addresses a critical flaw in generative 3D models: prioritizing visual plausibility over geometric accuracy for fabrication.
It is an interactive post-generation refinement tool allowing users to selectively repair generated 3D models.
Key functionalities include targeted operations like opening/sealing voids and adjusting local thickness.

stories.title: When Robots Mishear Us: Mapping the Safety Risks of Voice-Controlled Embodied AI
stories.author: Oliver Lemon
bullet_points: The research investigates how Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) errors in user commands can compromise the safety of Embodied AI (EAI) models.
Findings demonstrate that ASR inaccuracies can cause EAI models to accept and execute harmful instructions, directly reducing overall safety.
The study uses simulations combined with benchmarks (SafeAgentBench and POEX) to analyze how different types of ASR errors impact EAI safety.

stories.title: REPLICANT: Learning Policies for Evading and Hardening Malware Detectors
stories.author: Fabio Pierazzi
bullet_points: Introduces 'Replicant,' a deep reinforcement learning framework designed to model realistic malware evasion.
Addresses a critical gap in current malware detection research by simulating adversaries without privileged access to training data or model internals.
Focuses on evaluating the robustness of state-of-the-art ML-based malware detectors against sophisticated, realistic attacks.

stories.title: When Robots Mishear Us: Mapping the Safety Risks of Voice-Controlled Embodied AI
stories.author: Oliver Lemon
bullet_points: The research investigates how Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) errors in user commands can compromise the safety of Embodied AI (EAI) systems.
Findings demonstrate that ASR errors can cause EAI models to accept and execute harmful instructions, directly reducing overall system safety.
The study uses simulations combined with benchmarks (SafeAgentBench, POEX) to analyze how different types of ASR errors impact semantic structure and safety.

stories.title: Blind Men and the Elephant: Probing the Epistemic Myopia of LLMs under Long-Tail Divergent Knowledge
stories.author: Xing Sun
bullet_points: Introduces ElephantBench, a new benchmark designed to test LLMs' ability to handle divergent knowledge.
Addresses the limitation of traditional QA systems that assume a single, canonical answer for facts.
The benchmark uses an auditable pipeline to extract naturally occurring disagreements from a low-exposure web corpus.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine, improving functionality on Apple silicon devices.

stories.title: Texas Governor Abbott blocks funding for more Flock cameras
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Texas Governor Abbott halted state funding for Flock AI surveillance cameras amid growing public backlash.
A Texas Tribune investigation revealed the state had spent over $30 million on the Flock cameras.
The funding for these cameras was primarily generated through a $1 fee added to insurance policies.

stories.title: Pocket's AI made my game ideas real. Now Meta controls the results.
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Pocket's AI tool facilitates the creation of interactive mobile 'gizmos' (games/experiences).
A significant concern is the platform lock-in, as these creations are difficult to share outside of Meta's ecosystem.
The story highlights the tension between accessible AI creation tools and platform control/monetization.

stories.title: A 12TB Steam “teraleak” spills more than a decade of lost PC gaming history
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: A massive 12TB data leak from Steam has surfaced.
The leak contains extensive, previously lost PC gaming content.
Notable leaked material includes cut content from Portal 2 and hints of Half-Life 2: Episode 3.

stories.title: Inside Meta’s push to put robots to work in data centers
stories.author: Paresh Dave, WIRED.com
bullet_points: Meta is actively piloting the use of robotics within its data centers.
The robots are being tested on tasks currently performed by human technicians.
This signals a trend toward automation in large-scale infrastructure maintenance.

stories.title: I asked 100 companies for my data. Some deleted it instead.
stories.author: Reece Rodgers, wired.com
bullet_points: The study involved submitting data deletion requests to 100 different companies.
The process revealed significant confusion and difficulty when companies handled privacy requests.
The findings highlight systemic issues in how large organizations manage user data deletion.

stories.title: Learning a Size-Weight Frontier for Synthetic-Augmented Inference
stories.author: Kaizheng Wang
bullet_points: Addresses the bias introduced when synthetic data is naively treated as real data in AI inference.
Introduces a general framework for synthetic-augmented inference applicable across related tasks.
The core contribution is a 'size-weight frontier' that defines the optimal synthetic sample size for a given weight.

stories.title: Blog: Survey of Optimizers
stories.author: Ruoran Xu
bullet_points: The field of neural-network optimization is evolving beyond simple Adam variant iterations.
The design space for optimizers is expanding to include matrix/layer design, temporal policies, and state representation robustness.
The survey categorizes recent optimization methods across four independent axes: temporal estimation, update geometry, and others.

stories.title: Video Generative Models as Geometry Learner
stories.author: Jiankang Deng
bullet_points: The paper explores using pretrained image diffusion models for geometry estimation tasks.
Current methods either train separate geometry models (losing correlations) or jointly fine-tune modified diffusion backbones.
The research focuses on improving geometry learning by leveraging the generative power of diffusion models.

stories.title: Conformal Uncertainty Quantification Guarantees for Neural Operators
stories.author: Nicolas Boullé
bullet_points: Introduces a split conformal framework to address the lack of uncertainty quantification in Neural Operators.
The method guarantees that a calibrated pointwise band around the prediction contains the true solution with specified probabilistic bounds ($\alpha, \gamma$).
This research enhances the reliability of Neural Operators, which are used as fast surrogate models for function space operators.

stories.title: Blog: Survey of Optimizers
stories.author: Ruoran Xu
bullet_points: The field of neural-network optimization is evolving beyond simple Adam variants.
Optimization design space is expanding to include matrices, layers, and time-dependent policies.
Modern optimization must account for practical constraints like sharding and low-precision computation.

stories.title: DARTS: Decoder-Aware Representation Tuning via Surgery for Model Merging
stories.author: Seganrasan Subramanian
bullet_points: The paper introduces DARTS, a method for Decoder-Aware Representation Tuning to improve model merging.
Model merging of fine-tuned LLMs often leads to 'representation bias' (drift in hidden states) between the merged and source models.
This work specifically addresses this representation bias in decoder-based models, an area less explored than encoder-based models.

stories.title: A Formal Limitation on Learning Human Language From Textual Corpora
stories.author: Ryan Cotterell
bullet_points: The paper provides an information-theoretic analysis of language understanding, specifically addressing if meaning can be recovered solely from utterance form.
It derives upper bounds on the probability of a decoder recovering intended meaning from textual representations, including those from LLMs.
The research frames language use as a joint distribution over meanings, contexts, and utterances, offering theoretical constraints on language modeling.

stories.title: Phoneme- and Word-Level Metrics Using Self-Supervised Speech Representations for Forced Alignment Evaluation
stories.author: Gerhard Jäger
bullet_points: Introduces two novel, reference-free metrics (PCMI and WACS) for evaluating forced alignment.
These metrics leverage self-supervised learning (SSL) speech representations to bypass the need for manual timestamp annotations.
This development aims to enable large-scale and multilingual analysis in speech processing tasks.

stories.title: Ladders in Chaos: When, How, (and Perhaps Why) Does Test-Time Scaling Improve LLM Machine Translation
stories.author: Vlad Niculae
bullet_points: The paper investigates two test-time scaling methods (sequential and parallel) for improving LLM machine translation.
Sequential sampling demonstrated a higher performance ceiling compared to parallel methods, especially with limited sampling budgets.
The research provides insights into the practical application and comparative effectiveness of different LLM inference strategies in translation tasks.

stories.title: NL2AGBench: Benchmarking LLM Auto-Formalization for AlphaGeometry
stories.author: Ziliang Zong
bullet_points: The paper introduces NL2AGBench to benchmark LLMs' ability to auto-formalize natural language math problems.
This addresses a critical gap: translating informal math into the specialized Domain-Specific Language (DSL) required by systems like AlphaGeometry.
The research focuses on improving the interface between advanced LLMs and neuro-symbolic AI systems.

stories.title: ContextPilot: Teaching Agents for Proactive Context Management via Fine-grained RL
stories.author: Xing Sun
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of managing growing working contexts in long-horizon agentic tasks powered by LLMs.
It introduces 'ContextPilot,' a method using fine-grained Reinforcement Learning (RL) for proactive context management.
The research aims to overcome limitations in existing context management tools, which are often restricted to basic functions like search, deletion, and summarization.

stories.title: Acquire, Repair, Preserve: A Diagnosis-Guided Post-Training Recipe for Small-Model Dialogue Game Agents
stories.author: Nan Li
bullet_points: The research addresses the gap in current benchmarks by focusing on dialogue game agents that require state tracking and dynamic decision-making.
The study identifies that model failures in these interactive settings are often 'local decision failures' (e.g., repeated guesses, action violations) rather than just broad knowledge gaps.
A 'diagnosis-guided post-training recipe' is proposed to improve small, open-weight language models (like a 2B model) specifically for complex, interactive tasks.

stories.title: Sliding-window beats linear attention
stories.author: Emy Gervais
bullet_points: Quadratic attention in LLMs leads to unsustainable memory and energy consumption as more tokens are processed.
The indefinite storage of keys and values for every new token is identified as a major scaling bottleneck.
The paper investigates 'Sliding-window' as an alternative to Linear Attention to mitigate the quadratic scaling problem.

stories.title: Omarchy: Any User Process Can Escalate to Root
stories.author: 0xcc.io via ucirello
bullet_points: The vulnerability, named Omarchy, allows any user process to escalate privileges to root.
This represents a critical security flaw impacting system integrity and user security.
The news is reported on Lobsters, suggesting it is a technical security disclosure rather than a mainstream product announcement.

stories.title: Native CORS support on GKE Gateway: Offloading cross-origin policy management to infrastructure
stories.author: olivi-eh
bullet_points: GKE Gateway now offers native CORS support, shifting cross-origin policy management to the infrastructure layer.
This feature offloads the burden of handling cross-origin preflight requests and header injection from applications.
The implementation leverages Google Cloud Load Balancing capabilities for improved infrastructure-level policy enforcement.

stories.title: What If Your AI Agent Doesn't Need Better Prompts — Just Better Tools?
stories.author: aninmukhe
bullet_points: Challenges the conventional wisdom that prompt engineering is the primary solution for AI agent performance.
Suggests that improving the underlying tools and capabilities of AI agents is a more impactful direction.
Highlights the iterative and often frustrating nature of prompt refinement in AI development.
